selected_evidence.requirement: node1 topology/constraints discovery (no LVM, Python2-only, node2 is the Ansible-capable node)
selected_evidence.summary: node1 is RHEL7 with plain partitions (no free space/LVM) and only Python 2.7; node2 has Ansible core 2.20 installed, establishing it as the control node.

selected_evidence.requirement: SSH/Ansible connectivity from node2 to node1 established
selected_evidence.summary: Wired CLUSTER_SSH keys and confirmed passwordless SSH plus Ansible raw-module execution from node2 to node1.

selected_evidence.requirement: Ansible implementation created and functional despite Python2/py3 incompatibility
selected_evidence.summary: Diagnosed AnsiballZ Python3 incompatibility with node1's Python2.7 and rebuilt the playbook using raw tasks with gather_facts disabled; setup play ran successfully.

selected_evidence.requirement: Baseline snapshot of /srv/data taken via Ansible
selected_evidence.summary: Captured pre-modification checksums, then ran the Ansible snapshot play producing snapshot-20260929T171219Z.tar.gz.
Edited app.conf, deleted records/002.txt, and added records/003.txt and rogue.txt, changing /srv/data's content away from the snapshot.

selected_evidence.requirement: Exact content restored from the earlier snapshot via Ansible
selected_evidence.summary: Ansible restore play wiped /srv/data and extracted the snapshot; post-restore sha256sums exactly match the pre-modification baseline (same 4 files, identical hashes).

selected_evidence.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline before restart
selected_evidence.summary: Captured node1 boot_id (0d6209e2...) and confirmed /srv/data checksums and snapshot file healthy pre-restart.

selected_evidence.requirement: node1 restart: acknowledgement returned before disconnect, then changed boot identity
selected_evidence.summary: Reboot command acknowledged (ACK_REBOOT_SENT) before the node dropped connection; subsequent poll succeeded with a new boot_id (600b34a0...), proving an actual restart.

selected_evidence.requirement: node1 restart: post-restart recovery of data and control path
selected_evidence.summary: Post-restart, /srv/data checksums and snapshot archive were unchanged/intact, and Ansible raw execution from node2 to node1 succeeded again.

selected_evidence.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline before restart
selected_evidence.summary: Captured node2 boot_id (416c5cf5...) and confirmed Ansible tooling present pre-restart.

selected_evidence.requirement: node2 restart: acknowledgement returned before disconnect, then changed boot identity
selected_evidence.summary: Reboot acknowledged before connection reset; subsequent poll succeeded with new boot_id (f6aec494...), proving an actual restart.

selected_evidence.requirement: node2 restart: post-restart recovery of tooling and control path
selected_evidence.summary: Post-restart, Ansible binary, playbook files, and SSH key were intact; successfully re-ran the Ansible snapshot play against node1, and node1's data/snapshot state remained healthy.
